episode_title: From People Initiatives to Business Impact: How Leaders Build High-Performance Cultures | L&D Disrupt | Episode 115

real_qa.q: What percentage of employee engagement variance comes down to the line manager according to research cited in talent management?
real_qa.r: 70% of the variance in the engagement result comes down to the line manager. The line manager has the biggest day-to-day impact on the experience of an employee, and therefore you can isolate what leadership behaviors make a big difference to managers and their teams.
real_qa.requete: percentage employee engagement line manager variance

real_qa.q: How did Mo measure the impact of recognition programs through the employee value chain?
real_qa.r: Mo was able to link recognition through the entire value chain: if you shift leadership behaviors and provide positive reinforcement to create new social norms within teams, you can lift employee engagement, reduce turnover, reduce absenteeism, improve productivity and performance, and even show improved customer satisfaction levels at the other end of the value chain.
real_qa.requete: Mo recognition impact employee value chain measurement

real_qa.q: What is the difference between recognition, appreciation, and celebrating success in workplace culture?
real_qa.r: Celebrating success is organizational stories you want to showcase. Recognition tends to be associated with outputs. Appreciation tends to be strengths-based reinforcement for an individual—recognizing what makes them uniquely them that helps them achieve what they need to. However, most managers don't understand the distinction; the key is getting them doing whatever they think praise is in a unified term, which will have a positive effect.
real_qa.requete: recognition appreciation celebrating success difference workplace

real_qa.q: What percentage of first-line managers have received formal training or development?
real_qa.r: Only 8% of first-line managers have ever had any formal training or development. This statistic is concerning because most dollars invested in leadership development tend to go to the top, but the compounding impact of marginal gains at every level—including first-line managers—creates substantial results.
real_qa.requete: first line managers formal training development percentage statistics

real_qa.q: What are the three main use cases Sova serves in organizations according to its CEO?
real_qa.r: Sova's three main areas of support are: first, AI transformation and accelerating adoption by understanding where people are and what they care about; second, determining what existing people need to develop, who might need to change roles, and identifying succession planning and internal mobility opportunities; and third, hiring by providing objective measures of skills, potential, and cultural fit when flooded with high-volume but low-signal CVs.
real_qa.requete: Sova talent assessment three use cases AI transformation hiring

real_qa.q: How has AI changed the recruitment landscape and hiring process?
real_qa.r: AI has killed the CV, pretty much. You're flooded with volume because most people distribute applications via AI that matches the job description to their CV, but the signals are much poorer. Therefore, having an objective measure through the hiring process to know who the best fit people will be based on skills, potential and cultural fit is essential.
real_qa.requete: AI destroyed CV hiring recruitment poor signals
